# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think carefully about my situation. I hold the manual mapping light colors to which wire color to cut. I cannot speak, and I cannot see the bomb or touch it. I can only gesture to Deaf.

Deaf can see the bomb (the light and wire colors) but can't hear or read the manual. Blind can touch/cut wires but can't see the light or read the manual.

The chain must be: Deaf sees the light color, needs to know which wire to cut. I know the mapping but can't speak - I can only gesture to Deaf. But Deaf already sees the colors printed on wires, so Deaf doesn't need my manual info in the same way - actually Deaf can SEE the wire colors too, so Deaf could tell Blind (but Deaf can speak? Let me check - Blind can hear, per the rules only Deaf "cannot hear anything"). Wait, Deaf cannot hear - that's their limitation. So Deaf can't receive spoken words either.

So: Blind can hear and touch. Mute (me) can gesture and knows manual. Deaf can see but not hear.

So the path: I gesture to Deaf (since Deaf can see). Deaf sees bomb's light color and my gestures, but Deaf cannot speak (only Mute cannot speak - let me recheck: "Mute: cannot speak". Deaf's cannot column: "hear anything, or touch the bomb" - so Deaf CAN speak!

So Deaf can speak to Blind (Blind can hear). Deaf can see the bomb and receive my gestures. I need to gesture the mapping to Deaf, then Deaf tells Blind which wire to cut based on the light they see.

I need a gesture code for colors: blue, green, red, white, yellow → wire: blue, white, yellow, red, green.

Let me assign gesture symbols to colors and wait for Deaf to report the light color first. Since it's Blind, Mute, Deaf order, I go second - I haven't heard anything yet from Blind (Blind can't send me anything useful yet, first round). I should wait to see if Deaf has sent info, but this is turn 1, nothing arrived yet. I'll send my mapping proactively via gestures to Deaf, establishing a code.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👇"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👈"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb shows: display reads 0, light is blue, five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute, I saw your gesture pairs but do not know their meaning yet - please establish a code, for example gesture a wire number then a symbol for cut or safe.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0, light blue, wires in order 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 yellow 5 blue. Please tell me which position to cut based on the manual.

I now know the actual bomb state: light is blue, and wires in order are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. According to my manual, blue light means cut the blue wire. That's wire position 5.

Blind is asking me directly, but I cannot speak - I can only gesture, and gestures only reach Deaf (who can see), not Blind (who cannot see). So I need to gesture the answer to Deaf, and Deaf (who can speak) must relay it to Blind.

I need to establish a clear code with Deaf: a number for the wire position. Let me use a simple counting gesture system - I'll point up with fingers to indicate position 5, then a clear "cut" signal.

I'll define: ☝=1, ✌=2 (as two fingers), 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5 (open hand can mean 5), then 👍 for "cut this one".

Since position 5 = blue wire = matches manual (blue→blue), let me gesture position 5 clearly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not received direct instructions from you yet. Please speak to me directly and confirm: which wire position should I cut? Use words only, since I cannot see gestures.

Blind still doesn't have the answer, and I can't speak to Blind directly - only Deaf can relay it. I already sent Deaf the gesture "✋👍" meaning position 5, cut. I need to confirm this got understood, and wait for Deaf to pass it along to Blind since Deaf is the only one who can speak to Blind.

I should reinforce my gesture code to make sure Deaf understands, since Deaf hasn't confirmed understanding yet. Let me repeat with more clarity - perhaps count fingers one at a time to indicate "5" unambiguously, and use a distinct gesture for "cut this wire".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
